entities.title: Army-mediated talks on an interim government (9-12 September 2025)

properties.summary: After PM Oli resigned on 9 September and the army took security command, Chief of the Army Staff Ashok Raj Sigdel opened talks with Gen Z representatives and other stakeholders at Army Headquarters. President Ram Chandra Paudel joined the process, which moved to Sheetal Niwas on 11 September and ended with the agreement of 12 September on Sushila Karki as interim prime minister and the dissolution of the House of Representatives.

entities.title: Gen Z Discord session names Karki for interim prime minister

properties.summary: On the Youth Against Corruption Discord server, moderated by Hami Nepal and livestreamed on YouTube, thousands of Gen Z participants debated who should lead an interim government. Karki was chosen: Al Jazeera and Wikipedia give a five-name shortlist (Karki, Timalsina, Dhakal, Sampang, Pun) with Karki on 3,833 of 7,713 votes; The Tribune gives a different runner-up. Timing of the vote is reported inconsistently.

evidence.note: Setopati (published 10 Sept 19:36) already reports agreement on Karki after a five-hour discussion; Wikipedia says the vote was around 22:00 NPT on 10 Sept; The Kathmandu Post (30 Sept) says Gen Z representatives nominated Karki at 7 pm on 11 Sept after nine hours of discussion at Army Headquarters. Runner-up in the poll: Balen Shah at 28% (Tribune/PTI) versus Timalsina at 26.22% (Wikipedia table; Shah not shortlisted per Al Jazeera).

entities.title: Gen Z groups and Mayor Sampang meet the army chief at Army Headquarters

properties.summary: On 10 September, groups claiming to represent Gen Z, and Dharan Mayor Harka Sampang, went to Army Headquarters to talk to Chief of the Army Staff Sigdel. One group left after Sigdel asked them to sit with Durga Prasai and representatives of the Rastriya Swatantra Party. Crowds outside chanted different names (Karki, Balen Shah, Harka Sampang) and soldiers told them to agree among themselves and return the next day.

properties.summary: On the night of 10 September, KP Sharma Oli addressed a letter to "Dear Gen Z kids" stating that he was at the Shivapuri barracks, denying reports that he had fled the country. Setopati reported that Oli, Pushpa Kamal Dahal, Madhav Kumar Nepal and several ministers had been kept at the army centre for their safety.

The venue moved from Army Headquarters to the President's Sheetal Niwas on Thursday.

entities.title: Night consultations with party leaders at Sheetal Niwas

properties.summary: From Thursday night into Friday morning talks at Sheetal Niwas ended without resolution. President Paudel invited Maoist Centre chairman Pushpa Kamal Dahal on Thursday evening and Congress leaders were contacted by phone around 11 pm. Parties signalled support for Karki but wanted parliament kept.

entities.title: Friday talks at Sheetal Niwas agree on Karki and dissolution

properties.summary: On Friday 12 September, after a meeting postponed from 9 am, the President, army chief, Chief Justice Prakash Man Singh Raut, Maoist Centre leaders, Gen Z representatives and constitutional experts reached agreement: Karki as interim prime minister and dissolution of the House of Representatives. Sudan Gurung reportedly insisted on dissolution first; the army chief reportedly warned an emergency might be declared if no government was in place by evening.

properties.summary: Parliament was dissolved with effect from 11 pm on 12 September under a notification of the President's Office, on the recommendation of the interim government approved at Karki's first cabinet meeting. President Paudel announced fresh elections for 5 March 2026. Nepali Congress, CPN-UML and Maoist Centre called the dissolution unconstitutional.

entities.title: Karki was chosen through a Discord poll

properties.statement: Sushila Karki was chosen as interim prime minister through a public vote held by Gen Z leaders on Discord. Participants quoted by the Kathmandu Post call "the PM was chosen only through Discord" an overstatement: the army facilitated an agreement with the President and Karki also had support beyond youth circles.
properties.verification_note: Agency copy (ANI) and Al Jazeera present the Discord poll as the selection mechanism; The Kathmandu Post (Asia News Network repost) quotes Gen Z participants rejecting that framing, and its army reconstruction says the army facilitated the agreement with the President.

entities.title: Discord poll result: Karki 3,833 of 7,713 votes

properties.statement: In the open Discord poll Karki received 3,833 of 7,713 votes (about 50 percent). Wikipedia's table lists Rastra Bimochan Timalsena second (2,022, 26.22%), Sagar Dhakal third (1,098), then Harka Sampang and Mahabir Pun.
properties.verification_note: Totals appear in the Kathmandu Post and, with a candidate table citing ClickMandu and Al Jazeera, in Wikipedia. No platform data were published. Wikipedia and Al Jazeera put participation in the debate itself above 10,000 people, which is a different measure.

entities.title: Discord poll runner-up was Balen Shah (28%)

properties.statement: An online poll organised by Gen Z activists on Wednesday had Karki on 50 per cent, followed by Kathmandu Mayor Balen Shah on 28 per cent, then Harka Sampang and Kulman Ghising.
properties.verification_note: Contradicted by Al Jazeera and Wikipedia: the five-name shortlist was Sampang, Pun, Dhakal, Timalsina and Karki, Shah could not be reached by the moderators, and Timalsena is second in the Wikipedia table.

entities.title: Discord vote cannot be independently verified

properties.statement: Because Discord voting was anonymous, individuals might have voted more than once, and no official data from the platform exist to verify genuine participation.
properties.verification_note: The Kathmandu Post and Al Jazeera, citing different participants and a journalist, make the same point independently. It is an assessment, not evidence of manipulation.

entities.title: Dissolution of the House of Representatives is unconstitutional

properties.statement: The Nepali Congress, CPN-UML and CPN (Maoist Centre), and later eight parties jointly, said the President's dissolution of the House of Representatives on 12 September 2025 was unconstitutional. A commentator in The Wire describes the dissolution as applied under a doctrine of necessity that only partially wounded parliamentary democracy; President Paudel said on 14 September that the constitution had been saved.
properties.verification_note: Parties' position is on record on 13-14 September; ten writs were filed at the Supreme Court by 15 October. The Wire (19 September) argues the opposite. No court ruling was retrieved.

entities.title: Karki ineligible: non-member of the House and former chief justice

properties.statement: Petitioners argue the appointment of Karki breaches Article 76 (a prime minister must be a member of the lower house) and Article 132 (a former chief justice is not eligible for appointment to any government office). IANS reported on 13 September that she was appointed under the "principle of necessity".
properties.verification_note: Argued in writs filed at the Supreme Court (Kathmandu Post, 15 Oct); the question was flagged on 12-13 September by Al Jazeera and IANS. No ruling was retrieved.

entities.title: Dissolution demanded before the oath, carried out after it

properties.statement: Youth delegates and Karki demanded that parliament be dissolved before the caretaker prime minister was appointed, while the President argued dissolution would follow once the new council of ministers announced elections. Other reports say Karki was sworn in first and parliament was dissolved at 11 pm on her government's recommendation.
properties.verification_note: Nepali Times describes the order as the sticking point. Deccan Chronicle, ANI and The Kathmandu Post describe dissolution after the oath, on the prime minister's recommendation. Border Lens said the decree was drafted alongside the appointment letter.

entities.title: Army warned an emergency would be declared if no agreement

properties.statement: The army chief reportedly warned on Friday 12 September that a state of emergency might have to be declared if no government was in place by evening, which helped to clinch the agreement on Karki.
properties.verification_note: Border Lens attributes this to local media; Nepali Times and The Wire word it as "the military's warning" and "army officers apparently warned". No on-record army confirmation was retrieved.

entities.title: Army chief allegedly asked President Paudel to step aside

properties.statement: A senior journalist wrote on X that the army chief allegedly asked President Paudel to step aside so the military could negotiate, and that the President replied "I will not resign". Nepali Times adds that the army was criticised for detaining the President and not letting him take part in the talks.
properties.verification_note: Relayed by Nepali Times as an allegation; no other outlet retrieved repeats it and the army did not comment in the retrieved sources.

entities.title: Army plans to take over and restore the monarchy

properties.statement: Media reports and social media rumours on 11-12 September said the army was likely to take over and reinstate the monarchy, and that former King Gyanendra was trying to stage a comeback. The army issued a notice denying it and its chief told embassy attaches it was not a coup.
properties.verification_note: Rumour reported by ETV Bharat and Nepali Times; denied by the army's notice and by General Sigdel as quoted by The Kathmandu Post. Gyanendra rumours also debunked by Gen Z fact-checkers (see separate claim).

entities.title: Oli fled the country after resigning

properties.statement: Multiple reports on 9 September claimed that KP Sharma Oli had fled the country. Oli wrote on 10 September that he was at the Shivapuri barracks and had not left Nepal; Setopati and The Tribune also place him under army protection at Shivapuri.
properties.verification_note: Contradicted by Oli's own letter and two outlets. The Kathmandu Post (30 Sept) says Oli left the PM residence in an army helicopter, which is consistent with leaving the residence, not the country.

entities.title: Oli: lost power over his stand on Ayodhya and the borders

properties.statement: In a letter written from Shivapuri on 10 September, Oli said he lost power because he opposed the birth of Lord Ram in Ayodhya and insisted Lipulekh, Kalapani and Limpiyadhura belong to Nepal.
properties.verification_note: Oli's own statement as reported by The Daily Guardian; no independent corroboration of the causal claim was retrieved.

entities.title: Gen Z groups did not agree on Karki

properties.statement: On 10-11 September different groups claiming to represent Gen Z backed different interim leaders (Karki, Balen Shah, Harka Sampang); supporters of Shah and Sampang said they would not accept Karki.
properties.verification_note: Reported by Setopati, Ada Derana, Al Jazeera and Nepali Times independently.

entities.title: Balen Shah and Kulman Ghising declined the interim role

properties.statement: Nepali Times says Shah and Ghising were considered but both declined, possibly because they want to contest the next elections. The Tribune (PTI) reported conflicting media reports that Ghising might be appointed prime minister, and Al Jazeera says moderators could not reach Shah.
properties.verification_note: Reports conflict on whether Ghising was a live candidate; no direct statement from Shah or Ghising declining was retrieved.

entities.title: Balen Shah endorsed Karki on Wednesday 10 September

properties.statement: ANI reports that Kathmandu Mayor Balendra Shah posted on Facebook on Wednesday that he fully supported Karki leading the interim government. The Kathmandu Post (30 Sept) places Shah's support after Gen Z nominated Karki on 11 September at 7 pm.
properties.verification_note: Timing differs by about a day between ANI/Onlinekhabar and the Post reconstruction; Al Jazeera (11 Sept) already reports Shah voicing support.

entities.title: Death toll reported on 11 September: 30 to 34

properties.statement: On 11 September reports gave the protest death toll as 30 (Ada Derana), 31 (Al Jazeera, local media) and 34 (The Tribune, citing the health ministry).
properties.verification_note: Different tallies and counting times; superseded by the police figure of at least 51 on 12 September.

entities.title: At least 51 killed by 12 September

properties.statement: Police said on Friday 12 September that at least 51 people, including 21 protesters, nine prisoners and three police officers, had been killed since Monday.
properties.verification_note: AP, AFP, Al Jazeera and Deccan Chronicle report the same police figure; AP and AFP may share wire origin.

entities.title: Death toll 72 to 74 by 14-21 September

properties.statement: By 14 September Al Jazeera reported at least 72 killed; on 21 September The Kathmandu Post gave 74.
properties.verification_note: Counts rose as injured people died, and sources use different counting dates. First-day toll is also given as 19 (Post) and 21 protesters (ANI, Al Jazeera).

entities.title: Relief for victims' families: Rs 1 million or Rs 1.5 million

properties.statement: Karki announced on 14 September that families of those killed would each receive one million rupees; Setopati reported on 15 September a cabinet decision of Rs 1.5 million per family, including Rs 1 million as relief and Rs 500,000 for other expenses.
properties.verification_note: Possibly different items (relief versus total package) but sources frame it as the same payment.

entities.title: Sudan Gurung is not a Nepali citizen

properties.statement: Rumours said protest leader Sudan Gurung was not a Nepali citizen but from Darjeeling. Gen Z fact-checkers released a copy of his Nepali citizenship card in the Discord room and on social media.
properties.verification_note: Debunking reported by Al Jazeera only; the card image itself was not retrieved.

entities.title: Former King Gyanendra met the protesters

properties.statement: A claim circulated that former King Gyanendra had met the protesters. Gen Z organisers found that an old video of him interacting with youngsters was being shared.
properties.verification_note: Debunked by the Gen Z fact-check room as reported by Al Jazeera; Nepali Times separately reports widespread rumours of a Gyanendra comeback bid on 11 September.

entities.title: Cabinet expansion was done without consulting Gen Z

properties.statement: Sudan Gurung's group said on 14 September that the cabinet expansion was done without consulting them and demanded Karki's resignation. The Kathmandu Post and Al Jazeera that day reported Karki consulting a core Gen Z group and Hami Nepal members meeting on posts.
properties.verification_note: Gurung's group claims to speak for Gen Z; other Gen Z representatives were reported as consulted. Setopati notes the protesters "claim" to be leaders of the movement.
